title: Towards Formalising Schutz' Axioms for Minkowski Spacetime in Isabelle/HOL
relevance: Mechanizes an axiomatic event/path/betweenness presentation of Minkowski spacetime, including temporal order and explicitly layered locales; directly relevant to assumption-sensitive relativity.
limits: Read arXiv full text sections on locale/axiom encoding and reported results, not source repository or Isabelle session; no independent replay. Publication is a formalization report, not an ontological result.
authors: Isabelle paper authors as listed on arXiv
locator: Sections 3–5, especially locale hierarchy MinkowskiSymmetry/MinkowskiContinuity/MinkowskiSpacetime and stated omission/strengthening of assumptions
assumptions: Schutz event/path axioms encoded in Isabelle/HOL locales; the symmetry formalization chooses pointwise event invariance, stronger than a possible setwise reading; density is isolated in a separate locale where needed.
conclusion: Paper reports mechanized temporal-order and geometric consequences of Schutz's axioms; not a proof that actual spacetime has a preferred global time or that an ontology follows.
proof_status: Authors report checked Isabelle proofs; not reproduced in this audit.
dependencies: Isabelle/HOL; precise session and axiom closure not source-audited here.
open_questions: Locate/pin source archive; map each theorem to Schutz source locator and locale assumptions; inspect axioms/oracles and session imports; compare axiom variants and countermodels.

title: Using Isabelle to verify special relativity, with application to hypercomputation theory
relevance: Prior Isabelle formalization of first-order relativity theory and a no-superluminal-inertial-observer theorem; confirms long prior art for mechanized relativity.
limits: Paper-level inspection only; source, full dependency graph, and proof session not audited here. Authors' mathematical result is conditional on encoded axioms.
locator: Abstract and paper's formalization discussion; stated theorem: no inertial observer can travel faster than light
assumptions: First-order axiomatic relativity theory represented in Isabelle/HOL; the exact axiom set must be extracted from source before reuse.
conclusion: Authors demonstrate an Isabelle proof of the encoded theorem; no direct claim about temporal ontology.
proof_status: Authors report Isabelle proof; not reproduced.
dependencies: Isabelle/HOL plus project theories not enumerated in this screen.
open_questions: Find/pin public theory files and compare axiom variants against Andréka et al.; audit correspondence and assumptions.

title: AxQM: A Textbook-Scale Benchmark for Formal Proof Synthesis in a Library of Finite-Dimensional Quantum Mechanics
relevance: Public Lean benchmark with 1,019 tasks based on finite-dimensional quantum information, including a custom library and forked Mathlib; possible substrate for finite clock toy models.
limits: Repository README only; benchmark main branch leaves task proofs as sorry and solution library is private. No task declarations, branch build, license details beyond repository Apache-2.0 badge, or transitive axiom audit performed. GitHub reports one commit but page did not expose immutable SHA in this inspection.
version: main branch as viewed 2026-10-19; mutable; pin unavailable in page view
locator: README sections Contents, Tasks, Two benchmark regimes, Building; benchmark manifest and dependency metadata described
assumptions: Finite-dimensional quantum mechanics formalized in custom Lean library; benchmark statements cite Nielsen and Chuang items.
conclusion: Repository claims benchmark grading checks compilation, no sorry in dependency closure, and no new axioms; this is a benchmark specification, not independently verified here.
proof_status: No build; solution proofs withheld; public benchmark statements intentionally contain sorry.
dependencies: Forked Mathlib and Lean 4 per README; exact revisions require manifest/commit inspection.
open_questions: Pin branch commit and inspect imports, definitions, task declarations and mathlib delta; identify clock/unitary/POVM primitives; audit axioms and physical correspondence before using any theorem.
